n057695a1e4f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the evolution of MSME classification?
o: In 1950, a small-scale unit had an investment ceiling of ₹5 lakh.
The Industrial Policy of 1991 raised the investment ceiling for SSI units.
The 2006 framework prescribed separate limits for manufacturing and services.
The composite investment-and-turnover criterion was notified on 1 June 2010.
n057695a1e4f.x: The composite investment-and-turnover criterion was notified on 1 June 2020, not 2010. The other three milestones are correct.

nbeb82d1c68e.s:
Assertion (A): PMEGP is a credit-linked margin-money subsidy scheme for new micro-enterprises.
Reason (R): PMEGP is implemented by NABARD.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nbeb82d1c68e.x: PMEGP is indeed a credit-linked margin-money subsidy scheme for new micro-enterprises, but it is implemented by KVIC, not NABARD.

n4716df97d75.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 identified the handicaps of small industries as relating to:
o: Raw materials, finance, marketing and technology
n4716df97d75.x: IPR 1948 identified difficulties relating to raw materials, finance, marketing and technology.

nda3e174d06a.s: From 1 April 2025, a small enterprise has limits of investment and turnover up to:
nda3e174d06a.x: The revised limits for a small enterprise are ₹25 crore investment and ₹100 crore turnover (micro ₹2.5/10 crore, medium ₹125/500 crore).

n21f2cc0ac76.s: The RAMP programme for strengthening MSME institutions, market access and credit is supported by:
n21f2cc0ac76.x: RAMP is a World Bank-supported programme to strengthen Centre-State MSME institutions, market access and credit.

nc2abf48e7c0.s: TReDS platforms such as RXIL, M1xchange and Invoicemart, which discount MSME receivables, are regulated by:
nc2abf48e7c0.x: TReDS platforms are RBI-regulated and discount MSME receivables owed by corporates, government and PSUs.

nbf137e377a3.s: Reservation of items for the small-scale sector began in 1967 with how many items?
nbf137e377a3.x: SSI reservation began in 1967 with 47 items and peaked at about 873 items in 1984; the last 20 were dereserved in 2015.

n6723c93790e.s: Which committee on the MSME sector was constituted in 2019?
n6723c93790e.x: The U.K. Sinha Committee dates to 2019; Karve was 1955, Abid Hussain 1997 and S.P. Gupta 2001.

n162f0dbf57f.s: Under Chapter V of the MSMED Act, a buyer must pay an MSE supplier within:
n162f0dbf57f.x: Chapter V requires payment within 45 days, beyond which compound interest at three times the RBI bank rate is payable.

nb0d67271ae3.s: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, the sub-target for procurement from women-owned MSEs is:
nb0d67271ae3.x: The sub-targets are 3 per cent from women-owned MSEs and 4 per cent from SC/ST-owned MSEs.

nefbb57ec500.s: Which of the following was a feature of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956?
nefbb57ec500.x: IPR 1956 provided for licensing, public-sector expansion, small and cottage industries, balanced regional development and labour welfare. DICs came under the 1977 policy.

n71bddae1815.s: Formulation of India's FDI policy falls within the mandate of:
n71bddae1815.x: DPIIT's mandate includes FDI policy, Startups, industrial corridors and IPR matters.

ne2197b46f81.s: Which body was established under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 to speed up foreign investment approvals?
o: Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
Department of Investment and Public Asset Management
ne2197b46f81.x: The FIPB was set up as part of the liberalised foreign investment framework of the 1991 policy.

nb89d5118f1a.s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948, shipbuilding was placed in the:
nb89d5118f1a.x: Coal, mineral oils, iron and steel, aircraft, shipbuilding and telephone/telegraph apparatus formed the six mixed-sector industries.

nf95ede7505a.s: A criticism of the post-1991 industrial policy is that investment became concentrated in:
o: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha and Assam
Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
Kerala, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Bihar
nf95ede7505a.x: Investment concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, making regional imbalance a criticism.

n78c63bc3f52.s: The mandatory convertibility clause in the 1991 industrial policy framework concerned:
o: Rupee convertibility on the current account
Conversion of foreign equity into domestic equity
Financial institutions converting term loans into equity
Conversion of PSUs into joint-stock companies
n78c63bc3f52.x: The clause concerned financial institutions converting term loans into equity and was relaxed for term loans of less than 10 years.

necd70179b95.s: Under the New Industrial Policy, 1991, autonomy was granted to public-sector undertakings through:
necd70179b95.x: The 1991 policy granted PSU autonomy through MoUs, referred sick PSUs to BIFR and began disinvestment in 1991-92.

nc945a9c91a9.s: The MRTP Act was replaced by:
nc945a9c91a9.x: The MRTP Act was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, after the 1991 policy scrapped the MRTP asset threshold.

nf4f83a86aac.s: How many industries were reserved for the public sector under the New Industrial Policy, 1991?
nf4f83a86aac.x: Eight industries were reserved in 1991; this was cut to three and, after May 2001, to two (atomic energy and railway operations).

ne666e8462b8.s: Which industrial policy emphasised 'tiny' units, khadi and handlooms, and employment generation?
ne666e8462b8.x: The 1977 Statement emphasised small-scale and tiny units, khadi and handlooms, and employment generation.

nf6eef692379.s: The Industrial Policy Statement of 1977 was largely drafted by:
nf6eef692379.x: The Janata Government's 1977 Statement was largely drafted by George Fernandes, not Morarji Desai.

ndf2ca5db5bc.s: Schedule B of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 contained how many industries?
ndf2ca5db5bc.x: Schedule B had 12 industries to be progressively State-owned, with the private sector supplementing State effort.

n09c9c798783.s: DIPP was renamed the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) in:
n09c9c798783.x: DIPP became DPIIT in 2019, adding internal trade, traders' welfare and Startups; logistics was allotted only in November 2021.

n457a6b040ce.s: Schedule A of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, reserved for the State, contained how many industries?
n457a6b040ce.x: Schedule A had 17 basic or strategic industries under the exclusive responsibility of the State.

nfdb9f78ea6e.s: After 1991, many small-scale units were adversely affected by:
o: Import competition following removal of protection
A ban on imports of capital goods
nfdb9f78ea6e.x: Removal of protection exposed small units to import competition, which hurt many of them; SSI reservation continued after 1991.

naab3bc6309f.s: The MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29) provides for how many MSME parks?
naab3bc6309f.x: Policy 4.0 provides for 175 MSME parks, 'One Family One Entrepreneur' by 2030 and capital subsidy of 25% (45% for special categories).

n3b12ae877a2.s: District Industries Centres were created under the Industrial Policy Statement of:
n3b12ae877a2.x: DICs were created under the 1977 policy; the 1973 Statement identified a core-sector list and tightened MRTP.

n2cdb98ed898.s: After later reductions, compulsory industrial licensing under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 continues for how many industries?
n2cdb98ed898.x: Licensing was first retained for 18 industries and later cut to five: alcohol, cigarettes and tobacco, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, industrial explosives, and hazardous chemicals.

na9ba2225f33.s: District Industries Centres (1977) were set up mainly to:
o: Grant licences to large industrial houses
Provide one-roof support to small and cottage industries in each district
na9ba2225f33.x: DICs were established in every district to give integrated, one-roof support to small and cottage industries.

n76735162489.s: Which industry was NOT on the public-sector-only list of the New Industrial Policy, 1991 as originally framed?
n76735162489.x: Defence equipment, atomic energy and railway transport were on the public-sector-only list; pharmaceuticals were never reserved for the public sector.

n6cb4c6ed4b4.s: The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) was abolished in:
n6cb4c6ed4b4.x: FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and approvals moved to the FIF portal.

ned2050546a2.s: SICA was repealed and BIFR dissolved, with cases moving under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, in:
ned2050546a2.x: SICA was repealed and BIFR dissolved in 2016; pending cases moved under the IBC.

n61fc03676c0.s: Which committee examined insolvency and winding-up, leading to the NCLT and NCLAT?
n61fc03676c0.x: The Eradi Committee led to NCLT/NCLAT; Tiwari led to SICA and BIFR, Goswami studied corporate restructuring, Kohli sick SSI units.

n03dd5afeafe.s: Under RBI norms, a micro or small unit is sick if any of its borrowal accounts stays NPA for more than:
n03dd5afeafe.x: An NPA lasting more than 3 months marks a micro or small unit as sick (with 50% net-worth erosion as the other test).

nd5ac3fa1ec3.s: Obsolete technology as a cause of industrial sickness is classified as an:
nd5ac3fa1ec3.x: Obsolete technology is an internal production cause; poor working-capital management is internal finance, competition external demand, EXIM changes external policy.

n9489c20125c.shape: NOT (one-liner not buildable: only one false fact in original)
n9489c20125c.s: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of industrial sickness?
o: Bank loans turning into non-performing assets
Plant, land and funds lying idle
Increase in revenue receipts of the exchequer
n9489c20125c.x: Idle assets in sick units cause revenue loss to the exchequer, not an increase; NPAs, locked capital and unemployment are real consequences.

n1b0963e08ee.s: Under the new insolvency regime, the BIFR was succeeded by the:
n1b0963e08ee.x: BIFR was succeeded by the NCLT and AAIFR by the NCLAT; SICA's regime was replaced by the IBC, 2016.

n0debb182996.s: Under the original SICA, 1985, a sick industrial company had to be registered for at least:
n0debb182996.x: The original definition required at least seven years of registration, accumulated losses equal to or exceeding net worth, and cash losses.

n38317221094.s: The Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act (SICA) was enacted in:
n38317221094.x: SICA was enacted in 1985 following the Tiwari Committee (1984-85); BIFR was set up in January 1987.

n02fdb461c37.s: At present, delayed payments to MSMEs are addressed through:
n02fdb461c37.x: MSME Samadhaan handles delayed payments, while company insolvency goes to NCLT under the IBC, 2016.

n2fd47f65618.s:
Assertion (A): The Competition Commission of India functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
Reason (R): The Commission consists of a Chairperson and two to six members.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n2fd47f65618.x: Both are true (CCI, set up on 14 October 2003, is under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and has a Chairperson and 2-6 members), but its composition does not explain which ministry it falls under.

n99aadff85f6.s: Under the Competition Act, 2002, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
n99aadff85f6.x: Cartels, bid-rigging and price-fixing are anti-competitive agreements under Section 3; unfair pricing and denial of market access are abuse of dominance (Section 4), and M&A above thresholds are combinations (Sections 5-6).

n8268c5140df.shape: one-liner (sequence not buildable: too few dated facts)
n8268c5140df.s: Who was the first chairman of the Disinvestment Commission set up in 1996?
n8268c5140df.x: The Disinvestment Commission (1996) was first chaired by G.V. Ramakrishna; the 49% recommendation came from the Rangarajan Committee (1993).

n36110e12863.s: The New PSE Policy, 2021 classifies how many sectors as strategic?
n36110e12863.x: There are four strategic sectors (including banking, insurance and financial services), each retaining a bare minimum of 1-4 CPSEs.

nc1735edba24.s: The MRTP Act was enacted in:
nc1735edba24.x: The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969 and came into force in 1970.

nae9b65943f1.s: The National Company Law Tribunal was set up on 1 June 2016 under which section of the Companies Act, 2013?
nae9b65943f1.x: NCLT was constituted under Section 408; the NCLAT is under Section 410.

n1bd85c49d9e.s: DIPAM, which manages Central Government equity and disinvestment, functions under the Ministry of:
n1bd85c49d9e.x: DIPAM (renamed from the Department of Disinvestment in 2016) works under the Ministry of Finance.

n7a56f54da80.s: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) was dissolved on:
n7a56f54da80.x: BIFR, created under SICA 1985, was dissolved on 1 December 2016 and its cases went to NCLT/NCLAT.

nd5aa1771deb.s: The sale of government equity in public sector enterprises is known as:
nd5aa1771deb.x: Selling government equity is disinvestment; liberalisation is removal of licences, quotas and controls.

n1f5b0efb5fb.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 followed the Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee headed by:
n1f5b0efb5fb.x: The IBC was enacted on 28 May 2016 after the T.K. Viswanathan-led BLRC (2015).

nd2c5356f431.s: Which of the following is a disinvestment instrument used by DIPAM?
nd2c5356f431.x: CPSE ETF, Offer for Sale, IPO/FPO and strategic sale are disinvestment instruments; SLR, CRR and repo are monetary and banking tools.

n9231b124a9a.s: Leather was removed from compulsory industrial licensing in:
n9231b124a9a.x: Leather was delicensed in 1993; the five remaining licensed categories are alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, and industrial explosives.

n3b3607745b2.s:
Assertion (A): India's manufacturing strategy is criticised for missing its manufacturing target.
Reason (R): Manufacturing has already exceeded 25 per cent of GDP in all sectors.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n3b3607745b2.x: The 25 per cent of GDP target has been missed, which is a stated criticism; R reverses this and is false.

n0b524a015ca.s: In NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index (July 2026), Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
n0b524a015ca.x: Andhra Pradesh was among the Frontrunners (score 45-50); Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Goa and Odisha were Top Performers.

nae1a13a54e4.s: The SPICe+ reform was introduced to improve which ease-of-doing-business area?
nae1a13a54e4.x: SPICe+ supports starting a business; online building-plan approvals target construction permits, IBC insolvency and GST taxes.

nc490a5816e5.s: The PLI scheme for the automobile sector (PLI-Auto) has an outlay of:
nc490a5816e5.x: PLI-Auto has an outlay of ₹25,938 crore and requires at least 50 per cent domestic value addition.

ndfc6185cec6.s: In the proposed framework replacing SEZ rules, 'DESH' stands for:
o: Development of Export and Special Hubs
Development of Export and Services Hubs
ndfc6185cec6.x: DESH is Development of Enterprise & Service Hubs; it would drop compulsory positive NFE, allow DTA sales and be WTO-compliant.

n0c7b0175ca9.s: Under the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (FY2026-27 to FY2030-31), the extra incentive for domestic sourcing is up to:
n0c7b0175ca9.x: The scheme gives 2.25-5% on eligible sales, up to 1.5% extra for domestic sourcing and 3% extra for design and R&D by Indian brands.

n5b8d0296722.s: The National Manufacturing Policy, 2011 aimed to raise manufacturing's share of GDP within a decade to:
n5b8d0296722.x: NMP 2011 targeted a 25% manufacturing share of GDP within a decade and 100 million jobs.

n737dfd93b84.s: How many projects have been approved under the India Semiconductor Mission?
n737dfd93b84.x: ISM has approved 12 projects with about ₹1.64 lakh crore of commitments; capital assistance may go up to 50%.

n23f261b39bf.s: The SEZ Act, 2005, along with the SEZ Rules, came into force on:
n23f261b39bf.x: The SEZ Act and Rules came into force on 10 February 2006.

n47fb9430bbb.s: Which areas are identified as weak indicators affecting India's ease of doing business?
n47fb9430bbb.x: Contract enforcement and property registration remain major bottlenecks; digital literacy and export promotion are not cited.

ncfa4b9c3255.s: The Foreign Investment Facilitation portal was merged with the National Single Window System in:
ncfa4b9c3255.x: The FIF portal was merged with the NSWS in August 2022.

n0a878e89ff9.s: The logo of Make in India is a ____ made of cogwheels.
n0a878e89ff9.x: Make in India (25 September 2014) has a lion made of cogwheels as its logo.

n5121ae9c5da.s: India's rank in the World Bank's Doing Business 2020 report was:
n5121ae9c5da.x: India rose from 142nd in 2014 to 63rd in DB 2020; the report was discontinued in 2021 over data irregularities.

n407a3a08c11.x: PM GatiShakti came in October 2021; the National Logistics Policy followed in September 2022.

ne620fe738ed.s: Of the 355 provisions amended by the Jan Vishwas 2.0 Bill, how many were decriminalised?
ne620fe738ed.x: The Bill (introduced 18 August 2025, passed 2026) amended 355 provisions across 16 Acts and decriminalised 288 of them.

n531d6f9ba91.s: The outlay of PM E-DRIVE, launched by the Ministry of Heavy Industries in 2024, is:
n531d6f9ba91.x: PM E-DRIVE has an outlay of ₹10,900 crore; ₹11,500 crore was FAME-II, which it succeeded.

n6b3990560c6.s: Which of the following missions was launched first?
n6b3990560c6.x: Make in India came on 25 September 2014, before Digital India (1 July 2015), Skill India (15 July 2015) and Startup India (16 January 2016).

nfd9b8292820.s: Make in India 2.0 covers how many priority sectors?
nfd9b8292820.x: Make in India 2.0 covers 27 sectors: 15 manufacturing under DPIIT and 12 services under the Department of Commerce.

n708c6b29953.shape: NOT (one-liner not buildable: only one non-credited item)
n708c6b29953.s: Which of the following is NOT a reform credited with improving India's Ease of Doing Business?
o: Land records reforms through DILRMP and ULPIN
Removal of all foreign ownership restrictions
n708c6b29953.x: Faceless assessment, faster electricity connections and land-record reforms were credited; removal of all foreign ownership restrictions was not.

n5b8a4464f75.s: The India Semiconductor Mission functions under the:
n5b8a4464f75.x: ISM operates under the Digital India Corporation of MeitY and supports fabs, OSAT/ATMP units and chip design.

n99cca0a3ead.s: The three pillars of the World Bank's B-READY framework are:
o: Regulatory framework, public services and operational efficiency
n99cca0a3ead.x: B-READY rests on regulatory framework, public services and operational efficiency.

n044322737ee.s: Which of the following was specifically included as a measure in the National Manufacturing Policy?
o: Replacing industrial training with fiscal incentives
Restricting skill development to metropolitan areas
n044322737ee.x: Skilling of rural youth was specifically included among the policy measures.

n2e1fad459df.s: Manufacturing's present share of India's GVA is about:
n2e1fad459df.x: Manufacturing remains about 16.3–17.5 per cent of GVA, below the 25 per cent target, so the strategy has shifted to scale, design and global value chains.

n958b352c7ae.s: A large integrated industrial township with zoned land use, clean technology and social infrastructure is called a:
n958b352c7ae.x: NIMZs are conceived as large integrated industrial townships with zoned land use, clean technology and social infrastructure.

ne52682968ac.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)?
o: It has an outlay of ₹945 crore.
Start-ups receive the support directly from commercial banks.
It gives up to ₹20 lakh grant for proof of concept.
ne52682968ac.x: SISFS is routed through incubators (up to ₹5 crore each), not commercial banks; the other statements are correct.

nf49d36d4c06.s:
Assertion (A): An entity formed by splitting or reconstructing an existing business is not treated as a start-up.
Reason (R): A start-up may be constituted only as a private limited company.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nf49d36d4c06.x: Split or reconstructed entities are excluded, but eligible forms also include partnerships, LLPs and cooperatives, so R is false.

n2af853207be.x: Stand-Up India supports greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, trading and agri-allied activities through scheduled commercial bank branches.

n4c7d53196c9.s: The ₹10,000 crore Fund of Funds for Startups is managed by:
n4c7d53196c9.x: FFS is managed by SIDBI and invests through SEBI-registered AIFs, not directly in start-ups.

n04decbdd1cf.s: India's start-up ecosystem ranks ____ in the world.
n04decbdd1cf.x: India is the third-largest start-up ecosystem; DPIIT-recognised start-ups crossed 2.47 lakh by August 2026.

n20a0d4b94b1.s: The National Startup Advisory Council was notified in:
n20a0d4b94b1.x: The National Startup Advisory Council was notified on 22 January 2020.

n231f6d04715.s: Stand-Up India covers loans in the range of:
n231f6d04715.x: Stand-Up India covers loans of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore, while MUDRA covers micro units up to ₹20 lakh under Tarun Plus.

ne2ac60c601c.s: A deep-tech start-up retains start-up status for up to how many years from incorporation?
ne2ac60c601c.x: A deep-tech start-up qualifies up to 20 years and ₹300 crore turnover, against 10 years and ₹200 crore for an ordinary start-up.

n06064db02d1.s: Angel tax was abolished for all classes of investors in the Union Budget:
n06064db02d1.x: Angel tax was abolished for all investors in Budget 2024–25.

ne7de4247a73.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about BHAVYA?
o: It has an allocation of ₹33,660 crore.
It aims to establish 50 plug-and-play industrial parks.
It is implemented by NICDC through an SPV of NICDIT and a State agency.
ne7de4247a73.x: BHAVYA aims at 100 plug-and-play industrial parks, not 50; the other statements are correct.

n93e4cf7b0a4.s:
Assertion (A): Under Section 10AA, eligible SEZ units get 100% income-tax exemption for the first five years.
Reason (R): The SEZ tax holidays were phased out during 2010-2013 under a sunset clause.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n93e4cf7b0a4.x: Section 10AA gives 100% exemption for 5 years and 50% for the next 5, but the holidays were phased out during 2017-2020, not 2010-2013.

nindian-economy-18-4.s: India's first private-sector Export Processing Zone was at:
nindian-economy-18-4.x: Surat was the first private-sector EPZ (converted into an SEZ on 1 November 2000); Kandla was India's first EPZ.

n7995d16653c.s: Coastal Economic Zones were proposed under which programme's port-led industrialisation pillar?
n7995d16653c.x: The 14 CEZs, port-proximate clusters and SEZs, were proposed under Sagarmala's port-led industrialisation pillar.

ndb847e55ace.s: Which change is associated with the proposed DESH Bill?
o: A ban on Domestic Tariff Area sales
Mandatory positive NFE for all units
Immediate repeal of the SEZ Act by an enacted law
Removal of the positive Net Foreign Exchange condition
ndb847e55ace.x: The DESH proposal removes the positive NFE condition and allows DTA sales; it is still pending and has not replaced the SEZ Act.

nc4249d3e6de.s: An SEZ may be set up by:
o: The Central or a State Government only
The Central Government, a State Government or any person
nc4249d3e6de.x: SEZs may be set up jointly or severally by the Centre, a State or any person, including public, private and joint-sector entities.

nindian-economy-53-1.s: Kandla, Asia's first Export Processing Zone, was set up in:
nindian-economy-53-1.x: Kandla EPZ was set up in 1965 as India's (and Asia's) first; the SEZ policy came in 2000.

nd355ac9b5a8.s: The Orvakal industrial node in Andhra Pradesh is part of which corridor?
nd355ac9b5a8.x: Orvakal is on HBIC; Kopparthy is on VCIC and Krishnapatnam on CBIC.

nindian-economy-18-5.s: The Special Economic Zones Act received Presidential assent on:
nindian-economy-18-5.x: The SEZ Act was passed in May 2005, got assent on 23 June 2005 and came into force on 10 February 2006.

n38ba3ff5a7b.s:
Assertion (A): Phase I of Bharatmala Pariyojana was launched in 2017.
Reason (R): Its coverage extends to more than 580 districts.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n38ba3ff5a7b.x: Both are true: Phase I came in 2017 and covers 34,800 km across 580+ districts, but its district coverage does not explain its launch year.

n5ef44033c3f.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NIIF – Created by an Act of Parliament in 2021
n5ef44033c3f.x: IIFCL (2006) has been an NBFC-IFC since 2013; NIIF was set up in 2015 and NaBFID was created by the NaBFID Act, 2021.

n24995243bc0.shape: one-liner (sequence not buildable: too few dated items)
n24995243bc0.s: The value of National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 (FY26-FY30) is:
n24995243bc0.x: NMP 2.0 is valued at ₹16.72 lakh crore (including ₹5.8 lakh crore of private participation); NMP 1.0 was ₹6 lakh crore.

n948116b891b.s: The National Infrastructure Pipeline (FY2019-20 to FY2024-25) envisaged an investment of about:
n948116b891b.x: The NIP envisaged about ₹111 lakh crore across both economic and social infrastructure.

n34b38879b38.s: The National Logistics Policy, complementing PM GatiShakti, was launched in:
n34b38879b38.x: The NLP was launched in September 2022 to bring logistics cost to single digits of GDP by 2030.

n0fa322e43a2.s: The LEADS index, introduced by DPIIT in 2018, is modelled on the World Bank's:
n0fa322e43a2.x: LEADS is modelled on the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index, not the Ease of Doing Business Index.

nf1efaa8d3a6.x: Sagarmala (800-plus projects, about ₹5.8 lakh crore) was followed by Sagarmala 2.0 in 2025.

n9437bed0837.shape: NOT (one-liner not buildable: only one non-instrument given)
n9437bed0837.s: Which of the following is NOT an instrument of asset monetisation under the NMP?
n9437bed0837.x: NMP instruments include PPP concessions, InvITs, TOT and securitisation; cancelling public ownership is not one, since ownership stays with the Government.

o: Greenfield assets, with ownership transferred to buyers
Brownfield core infrastructure assets, with ownership retained by the Government
Brownfield assets, with ownership permanently transferred
Greenfield assets, with ownership retained by the Government
n0067314434c.x: The NMP monetises brownfield core infrastructure while ownership remains with the Government.

ne184dfa3ec8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's renewable-energy and climate commitments?
o: The 175 GW renewable-energy target related to 2030.
Under the First NDC, non-fossil capacity was to exceed 40 per cent by 2030.
The First NDC sought a 33–35 per cent cut in emissions intensity from the 2005 level by 2030.
The First NDC targets applied to the year 2030.
ne184dfa3ec8.x: The 175 GW renewable target related to 2022, not 2030; the First NDC targets were for 2030.

ncb1b7fc2a33.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
ncb1b7fc2a33.x: RDSS targets reduction of AT&C losses and smart metering; rural feeder separation is DDUGJY.

nd05c7279eda.s:
Assertion (A): At COP26 (2021), India declared a net-zero target for 2070.
Reason (R): India also announced a target of 500 GW of non-fossil-fuel capacity by 2030.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nd05c7279eda.x: Both are part of the Panchamrit commitments, but the 2030 capacity target is a separate pledge, not the reason for the 2070 net-zero goal.

ned089d8650d.s: The original 2010 solar capacity target of the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission was:
ned089d8650d.x: JNNSM began with a 20 GW target, raised in 2015 to 100 GW (40 GW rooftop + 60 GW large/medium).

nf0b76487dd7.s: APERC approved how much coal power through Section 63 DBFOO bidding as the first phase of Andhra Pradesh's plan?
nf0b76487dd7.x: APERC approved 1,600 MW, the first phase of a planned 5,588 MW by 2035-36.

n5f21fd001b4.s: The nodal agency of the Andhra Pradesh Solar Power Policy, 2018 is:
n5f21fd001b4.x: NREDCAP is the nodal agency; the policy notes the State has about 300 sunny days a year.

n58ee2385061.s: The Electricity Act, 2003 replaced the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 and the:
n58ee2385061.x: The 2003 Act replaced the 1910 Act, the 1948 Supply Act and the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998.

nc5330e02c9f.s: India's AT&C losses fell from 22.62% in FY14 to ____ in FY25.
nc5330e02c9f.x: AT&C losses fell to 15.04% in FY25, and the demand-supply gap fell from 4.2% to zero by November 2025.

nd43010410f8.s: India's strategic petroleum reserves provide about how many days of import cover (IEA norm: 90 days)?
nd43010410f8.x: India's SPR capacity gives about 9.5 days of import cover, far below the IEA norm of 90 days.

n4db0ef59148.s: PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh covers about how many pumps?
n4db0ef59148.x: PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh covers 2.93 lakh pumps.

n5d4d2677561.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 1991 New Economic Policy?
o: Full capital-account convertibility was not adopted.
Demonetisation formed part of the 1991 reform package.
FDI was liberalised through an automatic route in high-priority industries.
Devaluation, tariff cuts and removal of import quotas were external-sector measures.
n5d4d2677561.x: Demonetisation was not part of the 1991 package; India's demonetisations were in 1978 and 2016.

n2bdbe1a67af.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of India's 1991 balance of payments crisis?
o: The Gulf War led to a doubling of oil prices.
Current account deficits had been financed by foreign borrowing since the 1980s.
Remittances from the Gulf region rose sharply.
n2bdbe1a67af.x: Gulf remittances dried up rather than rising; the other three were causes of the crisis.

n67186ce6f15.s:
Assertion (A): Civil aviation saw the entry of private airlines after the 1991 reforms.
Reason (R): Power distribution underwent complete and uncontested privatisation.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n67186ce6f15.x: Private airlines did enter civil aviation, but power-distribution privatisation remained debated, so R is false.

nindian-economy-39-8.s: Reduction of tariffs and quantitative restrictions under the 1991 reforms is termed:
nindian-economy-39-8.x: Import liberalisation cut tariffs and QRs; de-licensing ended licensing, disinvestment sold PSE equity, globalisation integrated India with the world.

n5a134a72806.s: Under the post-1991 liberalisation measures, tax rates were ____ and the tax base was ____.
n5a134a72806.x: Tax rates were cut and the base widened, alongside scrapping MRTP asset limits, deregulating interest rates and allowing private banks.

n0dea1e2c345.s: Stabilisation measures under the New Economic Policy are essentially:
n0dea1e2c345.x: Stabilisation corrects short-term imbalances (fiscal deficit, inflation, BoP) through demand management; structural adjustment is the supply side.

n7f9b41dca6f.s: After the 1991 delicensing, delicensed firms got:
o: Freedom in pricing but curbs on expansion
Freedom in pricing and no curbs on expansion
Price controls but no curbs on expansion
Price controls and curbs on expansion
n7f9b41dca6f.x: Delicensed firms gained pricing freedom and faced no expansion curbs; licensing stayed only for a few (5-6) industries.

n0afbb9e1a99.x: Globalisation expanded trade and technology access, but imports grew faster than exports.

n77322e4e289.s: India removed its remaining quantitative restrictions on imports in:
n77322e4e289.x: The remaining QRs went in April 2001; average tariffs fell from about 125% to about 30% and general customs duty was later cut to 10%.

nc3c0489337c.s: Disinvestment of PSU equity under the 1991 reforms was first undertaken mainly to:
nc3c0489337c.x: Disinvestment was first used to bridge the fiscal deficit and only later for efficiency; nationalisation was not part of the NEP.

n6f1831def02.shape: NOT (one-liner not buildable: only one non-MRTP item given)
n6f1831def02.s: Which of the following was NOT removed from the MRTP framework by the Industrial Policy of 1991?
n6f1831def02.x: The 1991 policy abolished MRTP asset limits, pre-entry restrictions and merger/expansion controls; SEBI's statutory status was a separate financial-market reform.

nae8d810e0c9.s: During the 1991 BoP crisis, about how many tonnes of gold were pledged to the Bank of England and UBS?
nae8d810e0c9.x: About 67 tonnes of gold were pledged, an IMF loan was taken, and the rupee was devalued in two steps (1 and 3 July 1991).

nf213b2d5de5.s: The Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS) was introduced in:
nf213b2d5de5.x: LERMS came in March 1992 (60% at market rate, 40% at official rate); a unified market rate followed in March 1993.

n17422fda018.shape: NOT (one-liner not buildable: only one non-element given)
n17422fda018.s: Which of the following was NOT an element of the Washington Consensus?
n17422fda018.x: Privatisation, deregulation and property rights were among the ten Washington Consensus rules; expanding import quotas was not.

n50a2017c909.shape: NOT (one-liner not buildable: only one non-measure given)
n50a2017c909.s: Which of the following was NOT a fiscal policy measure of 1991?
n50a2017c909.x: The tax net was widened, not contracted; expenditure control, subsidy cuts and better tax collection were part of the package.

n75e9a77e40d.s: The Indian rupee became convertible on the current account in:
n75e9a77e40d.x: The rupee became market-determined in 1993 and current-account convertible in 1994; capital-account convertibility stayed partial.

n60d8d0a8d35.s: India's GDP growth in 1994–95 was about:
n60d8d0a8d35.x: Growth was below 1% in 1991–92, about 5% in 1992–94 and 6.3% in 1994–95.

nindian-economy-39-5.s: Integration of the domestic economy with the world economy, with greater participation of MNCs, is called:
nindian-economy-39-5.x: Globalisation linked India to the world economy through trade, FDI and technology flows and drew in more MNCs.

nindian-economy-37-8.s: Structural adjustment under the 1991 reforms is:
nindian-economy-37-8.x: Structural adjustment is long-term and supply-side, while stabilisation is short-term and demand-side.

n99c8ebb8542.s: India's 1991 balance of payments crisis was marked by:
o: Stable prices, rising gold reserves and a balanced budget
High inflation, low foreign exchange reserves and a large fiscal deficit
Low inflation, high reserves and a fiscal surplus
High exports, falling public debt and a current account surplus
n99c8ebb8542.x: The 1991 crisis featured high inflation, critically low forex reserves and a large fiscal deficit.

n647f34846cf.s: Which statement correctly relates Rajiv Gandhi's reforms to those of 1991?
o: Rajiv Gandhi introduced the complete 1991 package.
Liberalisation began in the 1980s, but the 1991 reforms were far more comprehensive.
The 1991 reforms merely continued an unchanged policy of the 1960s.
n647f34846cf.x: Some liberalisation began under Rajiv Gandhi in the 1980s, but the 1991 programme was much more comprehensive.

n33580fa3486.s: The post-reform Indian economy is characterised by:
o: Complete isolation and a smaller private sector
Replacement of private investment by foreign aid
Greater global integration and a larger private sector
n33580fa3486.x: The post-reform economy shows greater global integration and an expanded private sector.

n22af38e155e.s: Which statement correctly relates liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation?
o: Globalisation is an outcome of liberalisation and privatisation, with outsourcing as a major feature.
Privatisation is the outcome of globalisation, and liberalisation means only export promotion.
Liberalisation and privatisation prohibit international technology flows.
Globalisation is independent of both, and outsourcing is unrelated to it.
n22af38e155e.x: Globalisation is described as the outcome of liberalisation and privatisation, and outsourcing is its major feature.

n648f0e36a61.s:
Assertion (A): The four Labour Codes were operationalised from 21 November 2025.
Reason (R): Draft central rules for the Codes were released in December 2024.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n648f0e36a61.x: The Codes came into force on 21 November 2025, but draft central rules came in December 2025, not 2024.

nd6de1d8e755.shape: one-liner (sequence not buildable: Codes share dates)
nd6de1d8e755.s: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 is subsumed in which Labour Code?
nd6de1d8e755.x: The Code on Wages includes the Equal Remuneration Act; the IR Code has the Trade Unions Act, the SS Code the Employees' Compensation Act, the OSH Code the Factories Act.

n95dd407408a.s: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, the national floor wage is fixed by:
n95dd407408a.x: The Centre fixes the national floor wage; the Code also provides a universal minimum wage and bars gender discrimination.

n46f8ec21c67.s: Which was the first State to ratify the Constitution Amendment relating to GST?
n46f8ec21c67.x: Assam was the first State to ratify the GST amendment; GST follows the Canadian dual model and traces to the Vijay Kelkar Committee.

n33bdfdd1114.s: Fixed-term employment was extended to all sectors by the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Central (Amendment) Rules of:
n33bdfdd1114.x: The 2018 Amendment Rules extended fixed-term employment to all sectors and removed the termination notice for temporary workmen.

n8393856de91.shape: NOT (one-liner not buildable: only one non-credited item)
n8393856de91.s: Which of the following was NOT credited with improving India's Market Distortions Performance Index position?
n8393856de91.x: GST, IBC and trade facilitation were credited; restoration of import quotas was not cited.

nae6e81e9057.s: In the factor-market reform framework, the IBC and capital-market reform are classed as:
nae6e81e9057.x: The framework covers land (land-record digitisation), labour (four Labour Codes) and capital (IBC and capital-market reform).

n81c68296dfd.s: Next-Generation GST (GST 2.0), announced in August 2025, introduced a special slab for sin and luxury goods of:
n81c68296dfd.x: GST 2.0 brought rate rationalisation and a 40% slab for sin and luxury goods; input tax credit was retained.

n36551296c68.s: The National Monetisation Pipeline (₹6 lakh crore over FY2022-25) was announced in:
n36551296c68.x: The NMP was announced in August 2021 and covers core assets of central ministries and CPSEs.

n5a2f0ad2dd6.s: Under the September 2019 corporate tax cut, new manufacturing units were given a tax rate of:
n5a2f0ad2dd6.x: The 2019 cut set 22 per cent for existing companies and 15 per cent for new manufacturing units.

nb8154cbf8d2.s: Which of the following taxes subsumed under GST was a State tax rather than a Central tax?
nb8154cbf8d2.x: Central excise, service tax and CST were Central taxes subsumed under GST; State VAT was a State tax.

nindian-economy-15-5.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the GST Council?
nindian-economy-15-5.x: Article 279A provides for the GST Council; 246A gives the power to levy GST, 269A covers IGST and 366(12A) defines GST.

n72fcd070bf4.shape: NOT (one-liner not buildable: facts identify only the excluded item)
n72fcd070bf4.s: Which of the following was NOT on the Government's second-generation reform list in the cited classification?
o: Reform of government and public institutions
n72fcd070bf4.x: In that classification, Legal System Reforms were treated as outside the Government's second-generation list.

n15aa710acef.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's trade with China?
o: China supplies about 16% of India's imports.
China supplies APIs and solar cells to India.
India imports iron ore from China as a major item.
India exports iron ore, cotton and marine products to China.
n15aa710acef.x: India does not import iron ore; it exports iron ore, including to China.

n25c077903ed.s: Which of the following pairs relating to SEZs is correctly matched?
n25c077903ed.x: The SEZ concept came in EXIM Policy 1997–2002; the policy was announced in April 2000, the Act enacted in 2005 and the Rules notified in 2006.

n0c5f577b176.shape: one-liner (sequence not buildable: too few dated items)
n0c5f577b176.s: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 targets India's exports by 2030 at:
n0c5f577b176.x: FTP 2023, in effect from 1 April 2023 with no fixed end date, targets US$ 2 trillion of exports by 2030.

na59f5428aea.s: In foreign trade, 'direction' of trade refers to:
o: The money value of exports and imports
The balance between exports and imports
The country-wise or region-wise pattern of trade
na59f5428aea.x: Direction is the country-wise or region-wise pattern; composition is the items traded and volume the money value.

ne0a70b53c43.s: A tax levied on imports is called a:
ne0a70b53c43.x: A tax on imports is a tariff; an import quota is a quantity restriction and import licensing an administrative restriction.

n05209fada06.s: Export promotion of marine products is handled by:
n05209fada06.x: MPEDA handles marine products; APEDA (under the Department of Commerce) handles agricultural exports.

n8788f7ff2df.s: The theory of absolute advantage in international trade is associated with:
n8788f7ff2df.x: Absolute advantage is Adam Smith's idea; Ricardo gave comparative advantage based on lower opportunity cost.

n2b2054e38d9.s: According to the WTO (April 2025), India's rank among world commercial services exporters in 2024 was:
n2b2054e38d9.x: India was 8th in commercial services exports; 18th is its rank as a merchandise exporter. Its services share rose from 2% (2005) to 4.3% (2024).

n34d314ac4ba.s: In 2024, with a 2.8% share, India was the world's ____ largest merchandise importer.
n34d314ac4ba.x: India was the 9th largest importer (2.8%) and the 18th exporter, with its export share rising from 1% (2005) to 1.8% (2024).

n94f8202a13f.s: Net terms of trade (NTT) is calculated as:
o: Import price index / Export price index × 100
Export price index / Import price index × 100
n94f8202a13f.x: NTT = export price index / import price index × 100; gross terms of trade is import quantity over export quantity.

nindian-economy-39-6.s: India's SEZ Policy, aimed at export competitiveness and FDI, was announced on:
nindian-economy-39-6.x: The SEZ Policy was announced on 1 April 2000 to make exports competitive and attract FDI.

nindian-economy-54-5.s: Importing goods, storing or trading them, and then re-exporting them is called:
nindian-economy-54-5.x: Entrepot trade means importing, storing or trading and then re-exporting goods.

nb6d17386a3f.s: The 1991 New Trade Policy shifted India from import substitution and quantitative restrictions to:
nb6d17386a3f.x: The 1991 policy moved to a price-based regime, alongside a two-step rupee devaluation in July 1991.

naaef348414b.s: In FY 2025–26, India's largest overall trading partner was:
naaef348414b.x: China became India's largest overall trading partner, while the United States remained its largest export market.

n786d2b5d954.s: Which statement reflects recent changes in the direction of India's trade?
o: Crude imports were concentrated in a single source.
Labour-intensive exports and crude-import sources remained unchanged.
Labour-intensive exports shifted towards only the United States.
Labour-intensive exports shifted from the US towards the Middle East, Africa, Europe and Asia, and crude sources diversified.
n786d2b5d954.x: Labour-intensive exports moved from the US towards the Middle East, Africa, Europe and Asia, while crude-import sources were diversified.

n3fa1bb49183.s: The immediate effect of devaluation or depreciation of a currency is that:
o: Exports become dearer abroad and imports cheaper at home
Exports become cheaper abroad and imports dearer at home
Both exports and imports become cheaper
Export and import prices are unaffected
n3fa1bb49183.x: Devaluation or depreciation makes exports cheaper for foreign buyers and imports dearer at home.

n2538eb058e0.s: India's FTAs have been criticised mainly for:
o: Widening deficits with ASEAN, Japan and Korea, and weak utilisation
Eliminating the merchandise deficit with all Asian partners
n2538eb058e0.x: The criticism is that FTAs widened deficits with ASEAN, Japan and Korea and have been poorly utilised.

n0c0334de878.s: For trade and tariff purposes, a duty-free enclave in an SEZ is treated as:
o: A bonded warehouse under State control
n0c0334de878.x: A duty-free enclave is treated as foreign territory for trade and tariff purposes, though it lies within India.

nindian-economy-53-4.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: ECGC – Government-owned export credit insurance company
MMTC – Trading in minerals, metals and precious metals
STC – Export credit insurance cover scheme
NIRVIK – ECGC scheme enhancing insurance cover on export credit
nindian-economy-53-4.x: STC (1956) is a canalising agency for bulk commodities; export credit insurance is ECGC's role.

n501002dbf85.s: Which of the following export-import documents is wrongly matched with its purpose?
o: Letter of credit – Customs document for clearing export goods
Indent – Importer's order to buy goods
Mate's receipt – Ship's mate acknowledges goods loaded on board
Shipping bill – Customs document for clearing export goods
n501002dbf85.x: A letter of credit is the importer's bank guaranteeing payment to the exporter; the customs clearing document is the shipping bill.

ne23d1c067c7.s:
Assertion (A): EXIM Bank provides lines of credit, buyer's/seller's credit and project-export finance.
Reason (R): Export credit insurance is the principal role of EXIM Bank.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ne23d1c067c7.x: EXIM Bank (set up 1 January 1982) gives such finance, but export credit insurance is ECGC's role, so R is false.

n695af169380.s: FDI in most manufacturing in SEZs is allowed under the automatic route up to:
n695af169380.x: 100 per cent FDI is allowed under the automatic route for most manufacturing; SEZs are governed by the SEZ Act, 2005.

n0fb866cf8aa.s: Export credit insurance in India is provided by:
n0fb866cf8aa.x: ECGC provides export credit insurance; DGFT issues FTP authorisations and runs Districts as Export Hubs and the Export Promotion Mission.

n8b2cd611afa.s: FTP 2023 offers a one-time amnesty for export-obligation defaults under:
n8b2cd611afa.x: FTP 2023 includes a one-time amnesty for EPCG and Advance Authorisation export-obligation defaults, along with rupee trade settlement and new Towns of Export Excellence.

n245eeb28ebf.s: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 came into force on:
n245eeb28ebf.x: FTP 2023 came into force on 1 April 2023 and has no fixed end date.

na6c2cd977c0.s: EOUs, EHTPs and STPs are units that:
o: Export at least half of their output
Must be located only in SEZs
Pay full customs duty on inputs
na6c2cd977c0.x: These units export all their output, may be located anywhere and get duty-free inputs.

n4034eb6f7b8.s: The Export Promotion Mission, aimed at MSMEs and first-time exporters, is run by:
n4034eb6f7b8.x: DGFT runs the Export Promotion Mission, which merges Interest Equalisation and the Market Access Initiative.

o: Customs duty on imported inputs used in exports
n53acaf9d6b0.x: Duty drawback refunds customs duty on imported inputs used in exports, not income tax on export profits.

nindian-economy-28-4.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the IMF is wrongly matched?
o: Reserve Tranche – Unconditional drawing right from quota subscription
Rapid Financing Instrument – Rapid assistance for urgent BoP needs
Rapid Credit Facility – Concessional assistance to Low-Income Countries
IMF core function – Concessional lending to Low-Income Countries
nindian-economy-28-4.x: The IMF's core function is surveillance, i.e., monitoring global and member economies; concessional help to LICs is the RCF.

nindian-economy-25-6.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: Balance of Trade – Exports of goods minus imports of goods
Capital Account – Includes the Balance of Trade
Balance of Payments – Complete record of transactions with the rest of the world
Current Account – Includes the Balance of Trade
nindian-economy-25-6.x: The capital account covers cross-border capital movements; it is the current account that includes the Balance of Trade.

n407ec89eef5.s: Which of the following increases a country's external vulnerability?
o: Adequate forex reserves for import cover
Reduced reliance on volatile FPI and debt flows
n407ec89eef5.x: Greater dependence on hot money increases vulnerability; adequate reserves, low short-term debt and less volatile flows are safeguards.

nabb08c0cc26.s: In the balance of payments, reserve changes and official borrowing are examples of:
nabb08c0cc26.x: Accommodating transactions such as reserve changes and official borrowing fill the gap left by autonomous transactions.

n92ec1ca0ecc.s: Which of the following is a cyclical, not structural, cause of India's current account deficit?
o: Dependence on imported oil and gold
n92ec1ca0ecc.x: A temporary global slowdown is cyclical; oil and gold imports, weak export competitiveness and the savings-investment gap are structural.

naddefe5bab4.s: In the balance of payments, shipping, banking, tourism and software are classified as:
naddefe5bab4.x: These are non-factor services, part of invisibles along with primary (factor) income and transfers.

n202c7164b3d.s: India's current account surplus in the fourth quarter of 2023-24 was driven by:
o: A sharp rise in gold imports
A rise in crude oil imports
n202c7164b3d.x: The Q4 2023-24 surplus came from a surge in services exports, not from gold imports.

nb8c2fca0099.s: Which of the following is an IMF lending window for balance of payments support?
nb8c2fca0099.x: The Extended Fund Facility (like the Stand-By Arrangement) is an IMF window; RBI's swap facilities and SRVAs are not IMF instruments.

nindian-economy-25-5.x: The balance of trade covers goods only; services and transfers belong to the wider current account.

n1eb3d9fcd56.s: Which of the following is an expenditure-switching measure for correcting a BoP deficit?
n1eb3d9fcd56.x: Devaluation, like import tariffs and export incentives, switches demand from foreign to domestic goods; the others reduce expenditure.

n05d0406337f.s: India recorded a current account surplus for three consecutive years during:
n05d0406337f.x: India had current account surpluses for three consecutive years from 2001-02 to 2003-04.

n8c61dea4d12.s: Which of the following is NOT ordinarily a measure for correcting a BoP deficit?
o: Increasing government spending on domestic projects
n8c61dea4d12.x: Higher government spending raises demand and imports, so it does not correct a BoP deficit; the others can help.

ne9184aff7be.s: Which of the following is an expenditure-reducing measure for correcting a BoP deficit?
o: Tight monetary policy through higher interest rates
ne9184aff7be.x: Tight monetary policy reduces aggregate expenditure and imports; devaluation, import substitution and export promotion are expenditure-switching.

n20d969e1106.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about masala bonds?
o: They are rupee-denominated bonds issued abroad, with currency risk on the investor.
The name was given by the IFC.
Maharashtra was the first Indian State to issue them.
The first masala bonds were listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.
n20d969e1106.x: Kerala (2019), not Maharashtra, was the first State to issue masala bonds.

n2e0313aa7c0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about exchange-rate terminology?
o: Depreciation under a floating regime means more domestic currency per unit of foreign currency.
Depreciation and appreciation are officially ordered changes under a fixed regime.
Appreciation under a floating regime means less domestic currency per unit of foreign currency.
Official changes under a fixed regime are devaluation and revaluation.
n2e0313aa7c0.x: Depreciation and appreciation are market-driven changes under a flexible regime; official changes under a fixed regime are devaluation and revaluation.

n3f2d6fdd84b.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Revaluation – Official raising of the currency's value under a fixed regime
Depreciation – Market rise in the domestic-currency price of foreign currency
Devaluation – Official raising of the currency's value under a fixed regime
Appreciation – Market fall in the domestic-currency price of foreign currency
n3f2d6fdd84b.x: Devaluation is the official lowering, not raising, of a currency's value under a fixed regime; official raising is revaluation.

nf81b24d417d.s: India accepted IMF Article VIII and moved to current account convertibility in:
nf81b24d417d.x: India accepted Article VIII in August 1994, after the dual rates were unified on 1 March 1993.

n000492ba05c.s: The RBI instituted the SAARC Currency Swap Framework in:
n000492ba05c.x: The framework (2012) offers short-term BoP liquidity through bilateral swaps with the RBI, with a 3-month tenor rollable twice.

nindian-economy-47-6.s: Under a flexible exchange rate, a change from $1 = ₹60 to $1 = ₹65 is:
nindian-economy-47-6.x: More rupees per dollar under a floating rate is depreciation; devaluation and revaluation apply to fixed rates.

n9b515b212ab.s: Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs) are rupee accounts of:
o: Foreign banks maintained with banks in India
Indian banks maintained with foreign banks
The RBI with foreign central banks
n9b515b212ab.x: SRVAs are rupee accounts of foreign banks with Indian banks, enabling INR trade settlement; since 2025 surplus balances may go into corporate bonds and CPs.

n4cd864a427a.s: A rise in the rupee's Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) indicates:
n4cd864a427a.x: A rise in NEER means rupee appreciation, making imports cheaper and exports less competitive.

nf59dd8a0b2b.s: Higher imports may be accompanied by currency stability or appreciation when supported by:
nf59dd8a0b2b.x: Net investment inflows can finance imports, so higher imports do not always cause depreciation.

n82d58842c7d.s: RBI intervention in the foreign exchange market primarily aims to:
o: Defend a permanently fixed rupee-dollar level
n82d58842c7d.x: The RBI intervenes mainly to curb volatility, using reserves if needed, not to defend a fixed rate.

nd72a906ad0a.s: In a dollar-rupee buy/sell swap, banks:
o: Buy dollars from the RBI and sell them back later at a discount
Sell dollars to the RBI permanently
Sell dollars to the RBI and buy them back later at a premium
Buy rupee bonds from the RBI
nd72a906ad0a.x: Banks sell dollars to the RBI and repurchase later at a premium, injecting rupee liquidity without permanently altering reserves.

ncedb98c7e22.s: Which committee provided a roadmap for fuller capital account convertibility in India?
ncedb98c7e22.x: The Tarapore Committee (report of 31 July 2006) gave the roadmap; India has full current but only partial capital account convertibility.

ndbf1edf379f.s: FEMA, which replaced FERA, came into force on:
ndbf1edf379f.x: FEMA was proposed in the 1997-98 Budget and came into force on 1 June 2000.

n75ed946e4ae.s: Special Drawing Rights, popularly called 'paper gold', were created by the IMF in:
n75ed946e4ae.x: SDRs were created in 1969 under the IMF's First Amendment (agreed in 1967).

nf42e0e05ec5.s: Which of the following can limit the improvement in the trade balance after a currency depreciation?
nf42e0e05ec5.x: Depreciation can cause imported inflation, makes inelastic oil imports costlier and raises ECB repayment costs.

nindian-economy-47-5.s: The Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) is the NEER adjusted for:
nindian-economy-47-5.x: REER is NEER adjusted for relative price or inflation differentials between domestic and foreign economies.

n8e59c4ebde8.s: The rupee was devalued from ₹4.76 to ₹7.50 per US dollar in:
n8e59c4ebde8.x: This devaluation was in June 1966; the others were September 1949 (with sterling) and July 1991 (two steps).

nindian-economy-47-7.s: A rise in the Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) tends to:
nindian-economy-47-7.x: A rising REER means real appreciation, which tends to reduce export competitiveness.

ne260dd8e9dc.s: India's dual exchange rates under LERMS were replaced by a unified rate on:
ne260dd8e9dc.x: LERMS came in 1992-93, the unified rate on 1 March 1993, and current account convertibility in August 1994.

n6eabdc5c4d2.s: Large capital inflows tend to make a country's currency:
n6eabdc5c4d2.x: Inflows raise demand for the domestic currency and push its value up, an effect linked with Dutch disease.

nd59fa844fba.s: The rupee symbol (₹) was introduced in:
nd59fa844fba.x: The rupee symbol came in 2010, after current account convertibility (1994), the First Tarapore Committee (1997) and FEMA (2000).

nindian-economy-43-6.s: The Special Drawing Right (SDR), created by the IMF in 1969, was meant to:
o: Replace the US dollar in trade
Fix the world price of gold
nindian-economy-43-6.x: The SDR is an IMF reserve asset created in 1969 to supplement member countries' official reserves.

nindian-economy-47-3.s: Devaluation may improve export competitiveness because:
nindian-economy-47-3.x: A cheaper domestic currency makes domestic goods relatively cheaper abroad.

nb3772d370ea.s: The Smithsonian Agreement was signed in:
nb3772d370ea.x: The Smithsonian Agreement was in 1971, after Bretton Woods (1944) and before India's 1991 devaluation and 1993 unification.

nindian-economy-47-8.s: High inflation and a large fiscal deficit tend to ____ a currency's exchange value.
nindian-economy-47-8.x: Both inflation and a fiscal deficit can weaken a currency's exchange value.

nad5036a9154.s: The largest component of India's foreign exchange reserves is:
nad5036a9154.x: Foreign Currency Assets are the largest, followed by gold; SDRs and the reserve tranche are small.

n5a145455b88.s: Under a flexible exchange-rate system, the exchange rate is determined by:
n5a145455b88.x: Under a flexible system demand and supply set the rate; under a fixed system the government fixes it and the RBI intervenes.

n99f6780c423.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference at Yaounde (March 2026)?
o: It produced only a draft 'Yaounde package' and no ministerial declaration.
A permanent solution on public stockholding was achieved.
The e-commerce moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026.
Sixty-six members signed a separate E-Commerce Agreement barring duties on digital trade.
n99f6780c423.x: The permanent public-stockholding solution remained deadlocked at MC14.

nf63ac3c0fa0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about subsidy boxes under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Amber Box covers price- or quantity-linked support such as MSP, measured as AMS.
Blue Box covers direct payments under production-limiting programmes.
Green Box support is not trade-distorting and has no limits.
Blue Box support is subject to reduction commitments.
nf63ac3c0fa0.x: Blue Box payments are exempt from reduction commitments.

n012be0ccfa6.s: The first WTO Ministerial Conference was held at:
n012be0ccfa6.x: MC1 was at Singapore (1996), MC2 Geneva (1998), MC3 Seattle (1999) and MC4 Doha (2001).

nf2df7412b87.s: Trade-related investment measures are covered by which WTO agreement?
nf2df7412b87.x: TRIMS covers investment measures; TRIPS covers IPR, GATS services and SPS/TBT health and technical standards.

nindian-economy-13-6.s: GATS, TRIPS and TRIMS extended trade rules beyond goods as a result of which GATT round?
nindian-economy-13-6.x: The Uruguay Round expanded the framework beyond goods through GATS, TRIPS and TRIMS.

n9a9bd641ce8.s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, conversion of non-tariff barriers into tariffs is called:
n9a9bd641ce8.x: This is tariffication; developed countries were then to cut tariffs by 36% over 6 years.

nd1c2c12cfb6.s: WTO dispute DS456, which India lost to the US in 2016, related to:
nd1c2c12cfb6.x: DS456 concerned solar cells; DS541 (MEIS, SEZ, EOU) went against India in 2019 and the ICT panel ruled against India in 2023.

n07fb5d4687c.s: At MC14 (2026), India sought a permanent shield for public stockholding programmes like the NFSA along with the:
n07fb5d4687c.x: India and the African Group sought a permanent solution, which MC14 did not deliver.

n9d61cc9b207.s: The Director-General of the World Trade Organization is:
n9d61cc9b207.x: The WTO, headquartered in Geneva, is headed by Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala; India is a founding member of both GATT and the WTO.

n76ab42c3c3b.s: The WTO Appellate Body has been non-functional since:
n76ab42c3c3b.x: The Appellate Body stopped functioning in December 2019 as the US blocked appointments; India has not joined the EU-led MPIA (2020).

nab2d9e6b2a6.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted at:
nab2d9e6b2a6.x: MC12 at Geneva (June 2022) adopted the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement and a COVID-related TRIPS waiver.

n609b4bd2ce9.s: Phase 2 of the WTO fisheries subsidies negotiations, on overcapacity and overfishing, was at MC14:
o: Deferred to the General Council in Geneva
Referred to the Dispute Settlement Body
n609b4bd2ce9.x: Phase 2 was not concluded at MC14; it was sent to the General Council in Geneva.

n912ff00ddce.s: The WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement was concluded as part of the Bali package at:
n912ff00ddce.x: The TFA came from the Bali package at MC9 (2013); India ratified it in 2016.

nindian-economy-12-5.s: The World Trade Organization, which grew out of GATT's Uruguay Round, came into effect in:
nindian-economy-12-5.x: GATT dates from 1948 and the WTO from 1995.

n2a3a408a3ca.s: India's main concern about plurilateral initiatives such as the IFD and the E-Commerce Agreement is that they:
o: May fragment the WTO by moving away from consensus
n2a3a408a3ca.x: India fears plurilaterals may fragment the WTO by weakening consensus-based multilateralism.

n04acaf0aba1.s: The Doha Development Agenda was launched at:
n04acaf0aba1.x: MC4 at Doha (2001) launched the Doha Development Agenda and adopted the TRIPS-public health declaration.

n4c24fce9fbf.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies, adopted in 2022, entered into force in:
n4c24fce9fbf.x: Adopted at MC12 in 2022, it entered into force in September 2025.

n2b8d0c3d1b5.s: The WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions, in place since 1998, lapsed on:
n2b8d0c3d1b5.x: The moratorium lapsed for the first time on 31 March 2026.

naf2e2174c85.s: For geographical-indication protection, India relies on:
o: The Lisbon Agreement, of which it is a founding member
TRIPS, as it is not a member of the Lisbon Agreement
The Lisbon Agreement, applied only to farm exports
The Lisbon Agreement in preference to TRIPS
naf2e2174c85.x: India is not a member of the Lisbon Agreement on appellations and prefers TRIPS for GI protection.

nindian-economy-19-4.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: FDI – Lasting interest with management control, generally 10% or more of equity
Automatic Route – Foreign investment requiring prior government approval
FPI – Investment in securities below 10% of a company's equity
P-Note – Offshore derivative instrument issued by a registered FPI
nindian-economy-19-4.x: The automatic route needs no prior government approval.

n64c54e5bbbe.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about FDI?
o: It can help finance the current account deficit.
It is associated with stable capital.
Gross FDI consists entirely of fresh capital.
n64c54e5bbbe.x: Gross FDI may include accounting changes and is not entirely fresh capital.

n2aabe3ae1fc.s: Foreign Portfolio Investors in India must be registered with:
n2aabe3ae1fc.x: FPIs must register with SEBI and are overseen by SEBI and the RBI.

n0095650da90.s: The foreign investment cap in private-sector banks in India is:
n0095650da90.x: Private banks allow 74% (49% automatic); public-sector banks allow 20% via the Government route.

n11703da8280.s: FPI flows into India are significantly influenced by:
o: US Federal Reserve interest rates and global risk appetite
n11703da8280.x: US interest rates and global risk sentiment strongly drive FPI flows; a flight to safety can cause outflows.

nc5f232f7083.s: DPIIT, the nodal department for FDI policy and data, is under the Ministry of:
nc5f232f7083.x: DPIIT is under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry; its FIF Portal has been part of the NSWS since August 2022.

ne5fddb90591.s: Which of the following countries is NOT covered by Press Note 3 (April 2020)?
ne5fddb90591.x: Press Note 3 covers land-border countries (China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan, Afghanistan); Sri Lanka shares no land border.

nb54f57f93bc.x: India follows a negative-list approach; FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and DPIIT is the nodal department.

ncf90100d132.s: The headquarters of IRDAI is in:
ncf90100d132.x: IRDAI is headquartered in Hyderabad; Budget 2025-26 raised insurance FDI to 100%, and insurance is in the Union List.

n5871cc36cdd.s: External commercial borrowings, trade credit and NRI deposits are all forms of:
n5871cc36cdd.x: Foreign capital in India includes FDI, trade credit, NRI deposits and ECBs.

nindian-economy-19-5.s: In e-commerce, FDI is permitted under:
nindian-economy-19-5.x: FDI is allowed in the marketplace model but not in the inventory-based model.

nindian-economy-20-7.s: Foreign Institutional Investment (FII) is a form of:
nindian-economy-20-7.x: FII is portfolio investment, whereas FDI is direct investment in enterprises or sectors.

n02a319b90f4.s: Which RBI regional office received the largest cumulative FDI during April 2000–March 2015?
n02a319b90f4.x: Mumbai received the most, followed by New Delhi, Chennai and Bangalore.

n0aa1301ad33.s: Under the General Route, the overall FPI limit in outstanding Central Government securities is:
n0aa1301ad33.x: The General Route limit is 6% of Central and 2% of State Government securities.

ne4221d238b1.s: Under the automatic route, foreign direct investment requires:
o: Prior approval of the concerned Ministry
No prior approval, but post-facto reporting to the RBI
ne4221d238b1.x: The automatic route needs no prior RBI or Government approval, only post-facto reporting to the RBI.

n41b0d4e10a1.s: Google announced a $15 billion, 1 GW AI data centre in Andhra Pradesh at:
n41b0d4e10a1.x: Google's $15 billion AI data centre is in Visakhapatnam; AP's Industrial Development Policy 4.0 targets at least $10 billion FDI.

n6eac3fe240b.s: External Commercial Borrowings are regulated by:
n6eac3fe240b.x: FEMA, 1999 replaced FERA, 1973, and ECBs are regulated by the RBI under FEMA.

n6bde8791ee6.s: FDI in the defence sector is permitted under the automatic route up to:
n6bde8791ee6.x: Defence allows 74% FDI under the automatic route and up to 100% through the Government route.

nb08401b0c2d.s: The FDI limit in the insurance sector was raised to 74% in:
nb08401b0c2d.x: The insurance FDI cap went from 26% to 49% in 2015, 74% in 2021 and 100% in 2025.

n4f97ecc0f72.s: Hyundai's facility at Sriperumbudur is an example of:
n4f97ecc0f72.x: Greenfield investment creates a new facility; brownfield means acquiring an existing business (e.g., Vodafone-Hutchison Essar).

n9c5be931bbc.s: FDI in brownfield pharmaceutical projects is permitted under the automatic route up to:
n9c5be931bbc.x: Brownfield pharma allows 74% automatically (approval beyond), greenfield pharma and medical devices 100% automatically.

n35c39c7b4e4.s: Foreign Portfolio Investment was opened to India in:
n35c39c7b4e4.x: FPI was opened in 1992 and is regulated by SEBI under the FPI Regulations, 2019, along with the RBI.

ned0f392dfa4.s: Net FDI may remain weak despite high gross inflows mainly because of:
o: Exclusion of services from net FDI
Exclusion of all foreign equity from net FDI
Profit repatriation, outward FDI and PE/VC exits
Deduction of imports from gross FDI
ned0f392dfa4.x: Net FDI is reduced by profit repatriation, outward FDI by Indian firms and PE/VC exits.

n83aab0e8192.s: India's record gross FDI in FY 2025-26 was:
n83aab0e8192.x: FY 2025-26 saw record gross FDI of $94.6 billion, with net FDI of $7.6 billion.

na69cb57fc05.s: India's net FDI in FY 2024-25 was only about:
na69cb57fc05.x: In FY 2024-25 gross FDI was $81 billion but net FDI only $353 million.

nf11f05f6855.s: Which of the following about India's FDI policy is NOT correct?
o: Caps were raised after 2014 in defence, insurance and pension.
The e-commerce marketplace model permits 100% FDI via the automatic route.
All sectors are exclusively on the automatic route.
More than 90% of sectors are on the automatic route.
nf11f05f6855.x: Some sectors still need the Government route, though over 90% are on the automatic route.
